source: NCERT Class XII, Contemporary World Politics, Ch. 3 (US Hegemony in World Politics).

sections.heading: 1. The Rise of US Hegemony
points: After the Cold War (1991), the world became **unipolar**, with the **USA as the sole superpower (hegemon)**.
**Hegemony** = the dominance/leadership of one power over others.
The **First Gulf War (1991)** (against Iraq, 'Operation Desert Storm', UN-backed) displayed US military supremacy.

sections.heading: 2. 9/11 and the 'War on Terror'
points: The **9/11 attacks (2001)** on the USA (World Trade Center, Pentagon) triggered the **'Global War on Terror'**.
**Operation Enduring Freedom** — invasion of **Afghanistan (2001)** (against Al-Qaeda/Taliban).
**Operation Iraqi Freedom** — invasion of **Iraq (2003)** — controversial (no UN mandate; no WMDs found).

sections.heading: 3. Three Faces of US Power (Hegemony)
points: **Hard power (military)** — the USA's unmatched military strength.
**Structural power** — dominance over the world economy and institutions (Bretton Woods, WTO, the internet, etc.).
**Soft power** — cultural and ideological influence (media, lifestyle, ideas).

sections.heading: 4. Constraints and Responses
points: Constraints on US hegemony: **the US Constitution/institutions (separation of powers), the free market/private enterprise, and civil society/media**.
Others may respond by **'bandwagoning' (working with the US)** or **'hiding'** (staying low-profile).
The rise of **China, the EU, and other powers** challenges unipolarity over time.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Post-1991 = unipolar world (USA = hegemon).
First Gulf War (1991) = Operation Desert Storm (UN-backed).
9/11 (2001) → War on Terror; Afghanistan (2001), Iraq (2003, controversial).
Three faces of US power: hard (military), structural (economy/institutions), soft (culture).
Constraints: US institutions, free market, civil society/media.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Hegemony = dominance/leadership of one power**.
The **Iraq invasion (2003) lacked a UN mandate** (unlike the 1991 Gulf War).
US power has **three faces: hard (military), structural (economic/institutional), soft (cultural)**.
9/11 was in **2001**; the Afghanistan invasion followed the same year.
